summary: 1933 steel fire tower in Marinette County; the state retired it in 2016 and the county approved removal, but the registry still lists it standing.

facts.design: 80-foot International Stacy steel tower with internal corner-leg ladder (register); 1934 survey: square skeleton steel tower with enclosed cab
facts.status_note: Registry lists it standing. The county approved a removal plan in February 2016, and no source confirms whether it was carried out.

events.note: Erected November 1933 per the register; the Central US page also gives 1933.
A USGS station description from 1934 calls the tower the Cedarville fire lookout of the Wisconsin Department of Conservation.
DNR decided to retire all 72 fire towers statewide; announced December 17, 2015 (FOX 11) with closure set for the spring.
Marinette County committee approved a plan to remove the towers (Bay Cities Online report dated February 5, 2016); timing uncertain and no confirmed removal in these sources.

corrections.proposed: unverified: registry says standing; county approved removal in 2016
corrections.why: The registry lists Cedarville as standing, but the county approved a removal plan in February 2016 and the same registry marks the Middle Inlet tower as gone. No source confirms the current state.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 80 feet and the 1934 survey gives 79.5 feet. The story uses the register's 80 feet (24.4 m) and reports both.

sources.title: DNR Removing Fire Towers from Service

notes_for_editor: Current state is unconfirmed. The registry still lists Cedarville as standing while marking the Middle Inlet tower gone, so the Cedarville entry may be stale. A recent photo or county record would settle it. The DNR closure is dated by the FOX 11 article (December 17, 2015).
